title: Security Hub Failed Controls

compliance.assurance_rationale: Saved search evidence for SI-4 when alert outputs are archived.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:securityhub:findings` events with `Compliance.Status=FAILED OR RecordState=ACTIVE` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.149 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:securityhub:findings` traffic without `Compliance.Status=FAILED OR RecordState=ACTIVE`. Confirm UC-4.1.149 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:securityhub:findings` collected via Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`, Splunkbase 1876); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

description: UC-4.1.149 — Security Hub Failed Controls: queries AWS `aws:securityhub:findings` for search criteria `Compliance.Status=FAILED OR RecordState=ACTIVE` and returns actor, resource, and region context for compliance review and change validation.
value: On AWS, detecting 'Security Hub Failed Controls' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.1.149 drives high-priority compliance alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Enable securityhub integration in AWS and forward findings/logs via `Splunk_TA_aws` into `index=aws` with `sourcetype=aws:securityhub:findings`. Validate field extractions before alerting.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`, Splunkbase 1876) with the modular input for `aws:securityhub:findings`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `Finding.Title` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable securityhub integration in AWS and forward findings/logs via `Splunk_TA_aws` into `index=aws` with `sourcetype=aws:securityhub:findings`. Validate field extractions before alerting.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:securityhub:findings" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:securityhub:findings" Compliance.Status=FAILED OR RecordState=ACTIVE
| table _time Finding.Title Finding.Severity.Label Finding.AwsAccountId
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.149_security_hub_failed_cont_149"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:securityhub:findings` in `index=aws` to detect security hub failed controls. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS Security Hub console Findings for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `Finding.Title` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_149_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Notable-style table, severity timeline, single-value open finding count..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`, Splunkbase 1876) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of security hub failed controls so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
